description: DataRef.embedded.content_hash is present but does not match the SHA-256 of the decoded bytes for the declared encoding. Registry MUST reject with data_ref_hash_mismatch (NOT hash_mismatch, which is the body-level ProducerContent code; NOT invalid_signature). This is a DataRef-level integrity failure — the body's own content_hash and signature remain valid. See RFC-ACDP-0007 §5 'Distinguishing hash failures'. Decoding rules per RFC-ACDP-0002 §6.3: base64 → decoded bytes; utf8 → UTF-8 bytes; json → JCS canonical bytes. PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING: content_hash sits INSIDE the closed `embedded` sub-object here (RFC-ACDP-0002 §6.3), not at the DataRef root (§6.1). They are two distinct, independent fields and a DataRef MAY carry both (§6.3) — the root one is the consumer's post-fetch integrity check, whose generic wording covers location-form data as much as embedded, while THIS one is the registry's publish-time check on decoded embedded bytes (§6.6 check 8). An implementation whose `embedded` model lacks the content_hash member will fail to deserialize this fixture and reject it with schema_violation, never reaching check 8 — THAT IS A CONFORMANCE FAILURE, NOT A PASS, even though a harness asserting only 'was it rejected?' goes green; expected.checklist_step is the machine-readable assertion that distinguishes a real pass. The `embedded` sub-object is correctly CLOSED (additionalProperties: false, fixture schema-003); the member belongs in the model. Two independent implementations have now reported this same divergence — see the 2026-07-05 errata (commit 390f2d3), which resolved it by adding the member to acdp-data-ref.schema.json rather than by moving the field.
